utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Good morning, all of you. Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances for today starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours. Barney Thomas, Carmela Javier, and Dan Saxon for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to all. On behalf of Mr. Perisic, Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith, Tina Drolec, and Boris Zorko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic. I hope you had a very rested night.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I remind you that you are still bound by the oath you have taken to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please, you are yesterday just starting the summary of your case or you said something in relation to round up the case. I remind all of you that in the absence of Judge Moloto, we are sitting according to 15 bis today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour Judge David.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the last part of yesterday's session for the most part, Mr. Nikolic, you were answering questions by the Judges. All of that followed from that draft decision, which is an exhibit. I think this is --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will not be needing that exhibit for the time being. P730, just for the sake of the transcript, P730. You were asked several questions by the Judges. During today's hearing, I'll probably be going back to those topics through a number of other documents. There are a couple of things I'd like to clarify with you, specific answers, please. All of this follows from our last subject yesterday. General, do you know from what point in time VRS officers and SVK officers, former JNA officers were receiving salaries from the Federal Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salaries of the professional members of the VRS, former JNA men and the soldiers of the SVK continually received salaries from --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. From what point in time on. The armies were established in 1992. From what point in time on were these men receiving salaries from that source?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were receiving salaries even earlier on in 1991, and in 1992. The cycle was never broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The personnel centres were set up in November 1993. Did these men receive salaries even before the decision was taken to set those up?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on what decision? Based on whose decision were they receiving these salaries?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those men were receiving those salaries pursuant to a decision by the supreme political body and supreme military command in the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What political body?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until 1992, while the SFRY was still around, this would have been the Presidency of the SFRY. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia then came into being, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of the witness's answer because he trailed off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the federal government. I do apologise. Because the federal government is in charge of defence policies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We talked yesterday. We looked at that law, and we looked at all the elements that go to make up a salary. We had the rank, the position, years of service. We also looked at what all the other entitlements were that flow from one's status, professional status within the army. In order to be able to receive salaries as members of the VJ, do these men need to have their status formalised in any shape or form?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And had those men been members of the VJ would have taken a special decision to regulate their status within the service?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This applied to each member of the VJ. In order for these men to receive salaries, there has to be a document that is adopted regulating their status within the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where is that envisaged? What regulation?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on the VJ, earlier on it was called the Law on the Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At those offices of the VRS and the SVK who were receiving salaries even as early on as back in 1991 -- all right. I'm going to -- at this point in time when the JNA -- maybe it's my mistake, well, I don't know, it's when the JNA suddenly left the territory of the Croatian Bosnia-Herzegovina. Had they been members of the VJ, would it have taken a special decision to set up these personnel centres?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I understand your question. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the law regulates their status within the service, these are your words, sir, would a special decision have been required for someone who --

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'd --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: One speaker at a time, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why was this necessary to formalise this? Why did this require a decision by the supreme political body in the country for them to be able to exercise their entitlements, a special decision?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic reason and the most important reason for such a decision to be taken by the supreme political body and the Supreme Command was to make sure there were records regarding each and every member of the army, their whereabouts so that their status could be ascertained. No record, no man, no soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. You mentioned these records. I was reading yesterday's transcript and then the questions by Judge Moloto and Judge Picard. I'll try to sum it up: Why was it necessary to keep the files of VRS and SVK army officers, yet there was no need to continued to keep the records of those who had by now joined the Croatian Army or the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic reason for records like that to be kept, which is also a basis for regulating one's status within the service for the VRS and the SVK, this stems from the highest-ranking political bodies for the entitlements to continue within these two services in terms of their status and in terms of everything else that flows from the service. That was the basic reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you believe that there was a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Would the speakers please be asked to observe a pause and may they please speak one at a time in order to ensure an accurate interpretation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, we've been kindly asked by the interpreter to both ...

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you into politics at that time? Were you actively involved in politics? Can you tell us here, without speculating, what the motives might have been driving the politicians to adopt a decision like that? Did you perhaps receive any information to that effect from your own superiors, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I may have missed an answer, but if I missed an answer, then so did Madam Stenographer. I don't know if we ever got any answer to the questions about General Nikolic's involvement in politics at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll withdraw the question until later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. We'll be moving on to a different topic now and then later we'll be using some documents to return to what we have been speaking about now. Mr. Nikolic, let me start like this: Do you know that Mr. Lilic and the political leadership eventually adopted a decision with regard to the problem that we've been discussing? If so, when?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear you right. When President Lilic came --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was any formal decision taken by the top-most political leaders in the country to regulate the status of those men?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you and your administration involved in any way in preparing this opinion or proposal regarding that decision?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to see another exhibit now, P1873, please, an OTP exhibit. This is a document comprising several documents. I want to see the letter written by Colonel Milos Kosic.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Could someone please give me a hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, it's marked as P1873.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 1, please. And you can -- you can manually go through the other portions of the document. That's what we'll be talking about. What is this document? Just for the record, this is document by the Federal Defence Ministry, dated the 6th of October, 1993, to the office of the VJ Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document sent to the office of the VJ Chief of the General Staff dispatched by the Federal Defence Ministry, signed personally by General Kovac, the said chief. This is an opinion of the administration for system status-related issues of the federal defence ministry in relation to a draft order adopted by the General Staff of the VJ, including a request to present our opinion on the amendments to this order, asking also whether they had our approval for certain amendments to the draft order that was presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in English, too, please. This is 16534 [In English] 6534 are the last numbers because this is with ERN numbers in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is it that we see in front of us, and in what sense is this document part of what you spoke about earlier?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document the chief of the administration for system and status issue in 1992 from whom I took over expresses his views and suggestions concerning the order that was sent to us eliciting our opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you paragraph 2. I think that the English interpreters will be able to follow: "In this context and bearing in mind the responsibility of this sector and existing regulations from that area, we believe that there are no explicit legal grounds for such an order to deal with the issues raised. However, there is an apparent need for such a political decision to be made at the highest level of command and control, but it goes without saying that the possible implications that would result from this, especially from an international standpoint, will be assessed." At the time, you were in this administration but in a different sector; is that right? General, my question is: Can you comment and tell us what Colonel Kosic meant by this, and did you take part in drafting this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Kosic was the head the administration, and this was and personal view of the administration that I myself drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, when you say here there is no explicit legal grounds for such an order, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we meant by that was that in the then regulations in force, such as the Law on the Army and other bylaws, there was no valid or explicitly defined legal ground for this proposed -- for the proposed solutions contained herein. If I may explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sought to adapt the solutions with the existing provisions from the law on the service in armed forces, and we primarily wanted to use Article 4(2) --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slowly repeat the numbers of the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Can you please repeat the article numbers slowly and the legislature that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we tried to adapt these solutions to the existing provisions from the Law on the Service in Armed Forces, which was in force at the time. Those were, particularly, Articles 271, 284, 493, and 494 of the said law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do these articles refer to? What do they regulate?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 271 speaks about a possibility of sending or deploying personnel outside of the ranks of the JNA army. Article 284 similarly speaks about the sending and deployment of personnel outside of the JNA and the method for regulating their status in these organs that do not belong to the JNA. And Article 493 and also 494 stipulate the scope of responsibility of people in charge to establish the situation and the status in the service. Article 493, it says that the status-related issues for the people holding the ranks of General shall be regulated by the Presidency of the SFRY, whereas Article 494 says that other instances are in charge of regulating status-related issues for other personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you invoked these provisions in the Law on the Armed Forces, also incorporated into the Law on the Army that was later adopted?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are going to go through some of the articles of that law, but for now, I wanted to know what you meant by this second sentence where you said: "However, there is an apparent need for such a political decision to be made at the highest level of command and control." This has to do with my previous question and the objection that came from Mr. Thomas. So my question is: Why did you include this particular paragraph in your letter?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the problems were piling up in the aftermath of the adoption of the decision to transform the JNA into the VJ and the decision to pull out the units from Bosnia-Herzegovina within a fortnight, we were faced with the most critical problem and that was how to put in order and update the records, primarily those referring to professional servicemen, what to do, if you allow me to say so, with the basic database for those members of the army who either left the army or joined other armies; and that is the so-called DPP2 file which served as a database, like I said yesterday, for a centralised records of all army members. Also, one of the most sensitive questions that needed to be resolved was the status of those members of the JNA who stayed behind in those territories without having their status-related issues solved; and we expressed confidence that there was need for this to be regulated but that this, however, goes beyond the scope of responsibilities and authority of the Chief of General Staff. Therefore, we proposed that the Supreme Defence Council should use its prerogatives enshrined in the constitution and pass a decision on how to resolve the status-related issues of these particular type of personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say that a decision should be taken at the highest level of command and control, which particular body did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the draft of the Law on the Army and in the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia as well, which was promulgated on the 27th of April, 1992, this issue is regulated in that the army in peacetime shall be commanded by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia pursuant to decisions taken by the Supreme Defence Council. In the next article, it says that as for the engagement of army and use of army shall be subject to a decision by the chairman of the Supreme Defence Council but in accordance with the Law on the Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, this is not a criticism. What you told me, you could have just put it in one sentence, and I'm telling this for the sake of time.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The highest organ in this instance was the Supreme Defence Council and Commander-in-Chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I'm asking you a specific answer -- question, I'm expecting a specific answer. Now, can you please comment on the last portion of this paragraph. Why did you write the following: "... possible implications that would result from this, especially from an international aspect will be assessed." What did you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, bearing in mind that the then Yugoslavia was both under the sanctions and under various pressures, there was a tendency -- or, rather, we assumed that this approach might produce some political implications at that particular period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted to hear. We shall now move on to the next document. The subject is the same. Can we have, please, P1872 on our screen. It is actually a document that contains multiple documents, and I'd like that General and I go through all of those. Let us just wait for it to appear on our screens.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, can you tell me again what the number of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's P1872.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First we have the covering letter, and it says five attachments. Can you tell me more about the whole set of documents that we are going to discuss now?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 1 of this document, as it was customary, there was a communication between various chiefs, and here we have the Federal Ministry of Defence is being informed that the General -- the Chief of General Staff had approved a certain draft order provided by the administration for system and status-related issues of the Federal Ministry for Defence, and it goes on to say that some of the remarks had been accepted and then some were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now who have to page 2 in both versions, please. This document has three pages in total. General, can you tell us what this document represents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English translation should be ERN -- yes, we have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you yourself pointed out that this document contains three pages and an attachment, I see this as a preparation or a speaking note for the Chief of General Staff for the Supreme Defence Council that is expected to adopt a certain decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 1. I'm not willing to read it all together, but I would like you to comment upon it for the benefit of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 of this document, the Chief of General Staff would like to inform the Supreme Defence Council about the fact that following the decision to rename the JNA to the Yugoslav Army and the returning of its members in the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the open -- or the matter unresolved was the legal position and personal status of all active JNA servicemen, civilians, who have remained in the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Serbian Krajina, and he provided figures for both of these armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please look at page 2 in English, and I think it's also page 2 in B/C/S -- or, rather, the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can you please look paragraph 5. I'm going to read it out to the witness and then ask him to comment upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I'm reading at the bottom of page 2, and it reads as follows: "The relevant office of the Yugoslav Army would make all these persons available and send them to a special organ of the Yugoslav Army General Staff (Personnel Administration) based in Belgrade. Further procedure to organise and implement the departure of these persons and resolve their status in service while they're outside of the Yugoslav Army will be taken over by the authorised organs of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbian Krajina. All the rights of these active servicemen and civilians would be enjoyed in the same manner and scope as for other professionals in the Yugoslav Army." So could you please comment on what the document says. Is that a fair translation and does it tally with what we were talking about a minute ago in terms of looking for a solution to this problem?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. May I comment, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By all means. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are referring here to these persons at the Belgrade Garrison, and they're saying that an administrative body shall be set up, an organisational unit, to put these men together and send them to the VRS and the SVK. This is associated with the Personnel Administration, meaning that any further steps taken after these men were dispatched would be entirely for the VRS and the SVK. Chief of the General Staff emphasises, though, in terms of protecting the entitlements and rights of these men, the same status will be given to them as those in the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this also refer to persons who, at the time this document was produced, had long been serving in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 1 tells you exactly about what categories of persons we are looking at here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now please go to a chart that we can find on the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. A clarification, please for that answer. Is the witness referring to paragraph 1 of the page as it presently appears on the screen, or is he referring to paragraph 1 of the actual document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, when I asked you about the categories of persons that this draft decision is in relation to, and I asked you about persons who were at that time already members of the VRS, can you give us a reference for that? What exactly in this document tells us that the category includes these men?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about regulating the personal status of all active-duty military personnel from the JNA who now remained in the VRS and in the SVK. It is also in relation to those persons being sent to those areas at some later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Chief of the General Staff first takes the floor, he goes on to speak about that. Paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we now please go to the chart or the table with is on page 5 in the B/C/S document and page 6 in the English.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, all right. Thank you. What is this information that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an attachment to what the Chief of the General Staff of the Supreme Defence Council said. It gives you an overview of the numbers of active-duty servicemen in the VRS and the SVK. Should I continue to comment? Thank you. Look at this overview or list, we see exactly under Article 271, that was discussed a minute ago, how many men were sent and how many men were found in terms of those who remained in the area following the withdrawal of the JNA. Those were former JNA members who had joined the VRS. Similar information also applies to the SVK. The last thing we see is the total. If you want me to comment on the figures, please say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 8th of October, 1993. Based on this chart or table, can you tell us how many members were in the VRS, those whose status needed regulating on the day the chart was drafted, and how many of these men were in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the VRS, 2.630 men. As for the SVK, a total of 982 men. In total, 3.612 men for both these armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with this document and would now like to move on, finally, to Prosecution Exhibit P731. This is President Lilic's order dated the 10th of November, 1993. General, are you familiar with this document, and how does that compare to everything that we've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order by the supreme commander, the president of the Supreme Defence Council. In its preamble, you can see that it invokes a basis for an order like this to be adopted. Should I add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The basis is stated here, and it's all in evidence already. Therefore, there's no need to dwell on this. Could you please read paragraph 1 of this order. It's an order; right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does this order mean to the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Chief of the General Staff, this order is a basis and also an obligation to act accordingly, to act on this order. His tasks are set out here telling him what he should do in terms of regulating the status and entitlements of active-duty servicemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 states: "The General Staff of the VJ shall organ keep a special record on active-duty servicemen, contract servicemen, and civilian employees of the former JNA who remained in the territory of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and profession servicemen and civilians employed in the Yugoslav Army who were born in the former SFRY republics of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina and were admitted to military schools or joined the JNA from these republics." We talked about this yesterday, and even today you talked with these records. Does this have anything to do with the problem regarding these records? Is there a task being issued here in relation to these records?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said a number of times in answer to your questions, the records were the fundamental problem being faced at the time. Finally, the president of the Supreme Defence Council, the Commander-in-Chief, which I think is something of an unusual gesture for him to take on the responsibility to say exactly what this order regulates. So he states right at the outset that one must organise and keep special records. This is one of the fundamental criteria set out in this record. Special records, and I'm not going to read again what you just read. He also defines the categories of persons that this applies to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, the second part of paragraph 3: "Throughout this period, these individuals --" and probably means the people's whose records are kept -- or rather, I won't paraphrase this, no. Let me take a minute to read it. Where -- what -- which body is being established here pursuant to this order?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A body to regulate these issues that you quoted in paragraph 3, and the bodies named in paragraph 4 of this document. The president of the republic, the Commander-in-Chief, talks about the implementation of these plans to do with special, and then he goes on to emphasise personnel centres, not command centres, personnel centres. As for your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says -- I'm reading Article 3, the latter portion. "... these individuals shall retain all the rights pertaining to their rank and qualification, retain the salary that they had in the post they occupied before the current assignment, or they shall receive the salary envisaged for the new post, whichever is more favourable for the individual." What is this in relation to in terms of the reasons for the establishment of these personnel centres?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the president of the republic specifies that throughout the -- this time these persons would be keeping their entitlements according to their rank, and we talked about that yesterday. What does that mean? It's a salary that is rank based. There are a number of points that is awarded, and the salary is then calculated, and then the position within a group that the person was assigned to before they were ever dispatched or after they were dispatched, just incase this person suffers no detriment whatsoever and this person is now appointed to a different duty in terms of the salary that is due him under the law. What this does, in practical terms, is to protect all these persons to make sure they can exercise their rights and entitlements as defined here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are formal conditions created here for their rights and entitlements to be exercised that they had from earlier on?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's exactly what this order means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, sir. Tasks are specified here for the Chief of the General Staff in relation to these personnel centres. What I want to know is your comment on the last task set out here, the method of dealing with the status in the service and protecting the rights from their remaining service of these members and their families. Is that not one of the tasks for the personnel centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 4 of the order talks about that. It particularly points out for the implementation on certain plans for the work of these personnel centres, and there's a list of what they should do, and then hereby authorise the Chief of the General Staff to deal with such and such issues. And then finally where it goes on to say, this is the last sentence, the procedure to regulate their status within the service and to protect the rights and entitlements of these persons and their families. That is the fundamental tasks that the personnel centres are now facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, in your own words what did you understand these personnel centres to be and what did you understand their work to be?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By virtue of this order, the tasks and activities are defined that the personnel centres would be in charge of. That is why I said this order was peculiar - I do apologise for the expression - in the sense of being different from the other documents. This order gives the Chief of the General Staff a very say -- sound basis for regulating a whole number of other issues. The fundamental task and function of this order on personnel centres would be twofold if you asked me. The fundamental function, the decisive function, is to keep special files covering certain categories of persons as defined here. The other function would be to regulate their situation within the service in terms of their status, rights, and entitlements under the rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: President Lilic invokes the Supreme Defence Council and one of its meetings in the preamble to this order.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: President of the republic or his -- does the president of the republic have a military cabinet?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this military cabinet have some sort of legal service that is its component?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What exactly does this legal service or legal team do?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never studied their rules, the rules of their work. Nevertheless, their job would have been to prepare documents for the supreme commander, the president of the Supreme Defence Council, in keeping with the laws and the constitution, and, of course, in keeping with its own powers. Any document sent by the General Staff, the government, a ministry, or any other federal organ must, of course, be reviewed, co-ordinated, and agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, do you know, after the issuing of this orders -- order, if the personnel centres were set up and who issued this specific order?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the order of the Commander-in-Chief and, by his authority, the Chief of General Staff within the scope of responsibility conferred on him by the president of Yugoslavia, set up these personnel centres. The -- President Lilic's order did not specify the personnel centres. However, what he established were the 30th and the 40th personnel centres. These centres, pursuant to the order of the Chief of General Staff, became part of the personnel administration of the sector for system and status-related issue of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Later, in 1995, you went to the General Staff. We'll talk about it later, but let's just mention this thing at this point. When you went to visit those centres, can you tell me how many people you saw working there? Can you just illustrate the situation for us?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I assumed the duty of the chief of the personnel administration, as I said yesterday, and that took place on the 31st of December, 1998, I only had one personnel centre, the 30th Personnel Centre, as part might have administration, because the 40th Personnel Centre had already been disbanded at the time. The composition of that personnel centre, because I was in charge of administrative issues that were coming from the General Staff, actually amounted to 10 to 12 persons. As far as I remember, there were four to six officers, three to four non-commissioned officers, and the rest were civilians. I'm not talking here about the personnel who were given the function of commanding, but, rather, leading and directing people in terms of performing the tasks given to them, and that is what we mentioned a while ago, was to keep records and resolve status-related issues. If you would allow me, I would like to say that these were people within the general VES, which is the military speciality, i.e., people who were versed in finances or other areas or people who simply dealt with personnel issues. Non-commissioned officers were mainly involved in information technology work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person who was at the head of the 30th Personnel Centre? Who was his direct superior?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Biga, Milan, was at the head of this department, if I remember correctly. This personnel centre actually had only one department and one general sector, and I said that it numbered -- the staff numbered 10 to 12 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His post was called chief?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was chief of the personnel centre. And another person who was a lieutenant-colonel was the chief of the centre, and, as I said, the total number of posts in the centre was between 10 and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to whom was the chief of the personnel centre answerable to directly?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was directly responsible to the chief of the personnel administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at -- no. Before that, while we still have this document on the screen, item 5 of President Lilic's order reads as follows: "For the implementation of all the assignments from this Order that fall within the competence of the Federal Ministry of Defence, ensure full co-ordination and co-operation between the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army and this Ministry."

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we spoke about the responsibilities and competence of the Federal Ministry of Defence, inter alia, we said that one of its duties was to provide financial means and to codify certain issues. In that sense, president, as the Commander-in-Chief, requires co-ordination to be established and that it be implemented in practice by all these involved within their respective domains.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let us now move to another document, which I also think is important for this topic. That's P734. It's an instruction on how the personnel centres are going to function and operate. While we're waiting for the document, which is dated the 8th of December, 1993, I will first go through a number of items that I think were important, but before that, can you tell me who passed this document and what is its significance?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to an order issued by the Chief of General Staff, which was harmonised with an order of the chairman of the Supreme Defence Council and the Commander-in-Chief, the Chief of General Staff issued a task to the personnel administration to adopt, as soon as possible, instructions on the functioning and programme of activities of special personnel centres. And in the preamble, you can see on the basis of which laws and which orders these instructions were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a relatively long document. It's made up of several parts. The first part is called "General work principles." Then we have the next chapter, "Record-keeping." Third chapter is "Secondment and transfer." Chapter 4, "Special procedures for relating status-related issues and other rights." And the fifth and last chapter is "Repatriation and -- of professional soldiers and their transfer from the personnel centres." Now, my question, General, is, because I think that the first item explains the underlying reason for adopting this particular document. I'm not going to read it, but can you tell me this: Was it necessary to draft such a long instructions if -- to secure a proper functioning the army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I probably put a too complicated question to you. So for the purpose of regulating status and keeping records on members of the VJ, was this kind of instruction necessary?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment, but I'm not going to ask you to comment number 1, which I think is quite clear, but, rather, your comment on item 4, and I'm going to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see, Your Honours, item 4 in English, and it reads: "For people in the KC service of professional soldiers and civilians from entering into professional military service, resolving service status, promotion, exercising other service rights, and until cessation of professional military service shall be regulated in line with procedure and pursuant to the regulations relating to the Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me why was it important to say a thing like this explicitly in item number 4 of these instructions?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been emphasised here a necessity, or, rather, an obligation of high-ranking officers; and it refers to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Serbian Krajina whose duty was to regulate the service status of professional servicemen in these armies respectively and to follow up the procedures that pertain to the Yugoslav Army, the main reason being for them to be able to exercise their rights that they are entitled to as members of these army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But where are these members of the VRS and the SVK exercising these rights?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres in Belgrade. I don't know if I was clear, if you need any additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What institution specifically enabled them to exercise those rights? You said the personnel centre, but they were part of what?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every order relating to status-related issues, a copy of that order is provided to the financial and computing centre on the basis of which the person exercised these rights. If it's something to do with the salary, if you do with some financial matters, it goes there. However, if it has to do with some medical issues, it is sent to a department where this fund is going to provide solutions for these problems, and this department was part of the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm not certain. It might be an answer to the question, but the question that was posed was: "What institution specifically enabled them to exercise those rights? You said the personnel centre, but they were part of what?" So at present, the record shows that the witness's answer was an answer to the question. If that's what my learned friend was attempting to do then he needn't do anything more, but I just make that observation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have a minute to look at it, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I think that something was omitted from the answer, so I think the best approach would be for me to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General -- well, maybe it's not even necessary. Just a moment. Just a moment. I'll try to be as simple as possible. Which institutions -- in which state, in which country, did these people exercise those rights?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the computing centre?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was an executive body attached to Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this is a good time for us to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] court is adjourned we will return at 10.45. Court is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, Exhibit 191, the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have that on our screens, and we shall no longer be requiring the present document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you have that in front of you, P191. I'll be asking you a number general questions and not covering the document as a whole. What we see on our screens is the Law on the VRS, published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 1st of June, 1992. You commented on this article, actually, on day one of your evidence. This is Article 337, towards the very end of this document. I'm not sure about the ERN page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Just a second. We don't have the transcript functioning in my ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hold it a minute there because we're waiting for the LiveNote to start operating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Registry informed me that we will take a minute or two to restart the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: We are ready now to start. Mr. Lukic, continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, no need for you to be looking at the document, just listen to my question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] informed that you should repeat the beginning of your questioning because nothing has been incorporated into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I asked for Exhibit P191, it's on our screens. This is the Law on VRS, published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 1st of June, 1992. I'm not sure if you have a hardcopy in front of you, sir.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move on to Article 377, the B/C/S reference is 37 and the English reference is page 55.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 377, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll read this back to you. You just try and listen so there is no need for you to even look for it. After all, it's right in front of you on the screen.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are looking at the transitional and final provisions of this Law on the VRS. It says: "On the day this law enters into force active commissioned officers, junior officers, and army personnel of the Yugoslav People's Army, citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina will become active-duty officers and NCOs of the VRS. Those who are its citizens, as all the citizens of the other countries that were components of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, those who wish to serve in the VRS and whose service is required." Let me ask you, first of all, if you are familiar with the Law on the VRS.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What exactly does this article of the law regulate?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 377, transitional and final provisions, specifically regulates that on the day the law enters into force the specified groups of persons, and I'm not going to be repeating that because you've read it back to us already, under these conditions can now become active-duty officers, professional members of the VRS under certain conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. All right. My next question: Does this mean that from this moment on the Law on the VRS shall be applied in their cases as well?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the Law on the VRS specifically? Did it have among it's provisions something regulating their status as servicemen and the relationships within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The officers specified in Article 377, and I'm here focusing on the former JNA members remaining, who assigns them to particular posts, gives them certain duties or promotes them, for example, under the Law on the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on each person's rank, establishment position, the group they belonged to and how their position within the service is regulating. For example, if you have someone holding the rank of general, under the law of Republika Srpska, it would have been the Commander-in-Chief or the president of the republic who was in charge of that. And our solution was quite similar too. As for all other officers, the defence minister would have been in charge of those. In keeping with the law, he would have had the power to transfer his power to other persons, the Chief of the Main Staff of the VRS and the corps commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And who was the President of Republika Srpska, or, for that matter, the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that would be?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the establishment of Republika Srpska, the supreme commander at the time, as far as I remember, was Radovan Karadzic. Following a meeting of the Assembly, I think he was followed by Ms. Plavsic and after that Sarvic, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an Assembly meeting that was held deciding that the post should be filled by colonel-general at the time, Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the Republic of Serbian Krajina have it's own supreme commander and commander of the Main Staff as well?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who these people were?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of who they were at one point in time. I can't remember the exact date though. For a while this was Martic, and then there was Babic for a period of time as well. As for the first commander of the SVK, it was General Milan Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us please now go back to the instructions that we -- guidelines that we discussed a while ago concerning the work of the special personnel centres.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll probably have to take a minute to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there any reference in this document to the service of these persons in the VRS or the SVK, how they were appointed, how they were promoted, what their careers were like in these two armies.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The guidelines on -- on the functioning and work of the special personnel centres. If you go back to that, you look at it, does it say anything about the way these persons are now appointed to their posts or promoted or how their careers should evolve now that they are members of the VRS or the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there's an additional explanation, if I may. The guidelines regulate, generally speaking, the status of all men in the VRS and the SVK. All men. No exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that wasn't my question. That wasn't my question. My question is, and please listen carefully, do these guidelines mention anything or refer to how they should be moving about within the -- their service in the VRS or the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Sorry. I didn't understand that the first time round.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It may have been my fault. I'm sorry. Who regulates their movement within the service and their status within the service specifically in the VRS and the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that happens in terms of their careers within these two armies, the VRS and the SVK, is within the sole remit of the relevant officers who are in charge, and they have to do this in keeping with the regulations that applied to both the VRS and the SVK, and it all has to be in keeping with their laws and constitutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The relevant officers of which army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like, for example, we said a while ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which armies?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the VRS, it would have been the supreme commander, the president of the republic for anyone holding the rank of general. For everyone else, the person responsible would have been the defence minister who, however, transferred his powers or his powers to other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One correction in the transcript. Page 33, line 6. When I asked the witness a question, he said no, which was not recorded in the transcript. And then later on he gave an answer. That was page 33, line 1, as a matter of fact. Part of the witness's answer. I asked him a question. The witness said, "No." If need be, I can repeat my question, but I think everyone heard it loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we spoke about the drafting of solutions for regulating status-related issues of these personnel and about record-keeping, you mentioned that adaptations were made in order to put in line these issue with certain regulations and later with the Law on Yugoslavia. What did you mean by that? In what way were the status-related issues of these personnel adapted to the solutions provided in the law?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had in mind the provisions of the Law on the Yugoslav Army that govern what is considered to be a military service, what is considered to be service outside of the JNA or the VJ, what is considered the system of salary payments. I was referring to responsibilities. I was referring to the conditions that someone has to fulfil to become a professional active serviceman. I was referring to the time required to spend in a certain post with a certain rank to become eligible for promotion. I was referring to specify characteristics of one military service in a specific army, and I was referring to the VRS that can affect on the overall military service. I was referring to the method of applying certain regulation that define the right to salary under the Law on the VJ, and I analysed the provisions of this law that you just mentioned. I found that the solutions were almost identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more question to make it all clear. We have seen the table pertaining to October 1993, which shows the number of the so-called former JNA who became members of the VRS and SVK either from the beginning or was sent later. Did these men, did all members of the VRS, or did all officers of the VRS, or only specific categories, received their salaries through the personnel centre? If you can say which particular categories, if that would be your answer.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to try and give you two answers, because there are two questions in your question. According to what I know, the numerical strengths of the VRS was between 200 and 250.000 troops, including military personnel, i.e., around 15.000 commissioned officers and 15.000 non-commissioned officers. I'm sorry, I'm not sure about the exact figure. However, from this table we saw that the minimum number was given who were entitled to receive salaries. The total number concerning the whole period varies between 4.000 and 4.700, including the civilians in the -- that were payable by the VJ, and the Army of Serbian Krajina never exceeded the figure of 4.000. So if you compare the overall number of personnel in the army, this is really a minimum number of servicemen entitled to receive this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 35, line 8, you said 4.000 and 4.700, including the civilians, and you mentioned the VRS.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was speaking only about the VRS. And the total number of the Army of the SVK never exceeded 4.000.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the numbers of the VRS army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [In English] 65 ter 00470D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, General, if you will be able to find it in your binder.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I don't know how the Chamber will be able to deal with this translation of the document, because we don't have figures in the translation, but first of all, tell us something about this document. Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was produced by the administration for system and status-related issues of the federal MOD, which was under my jurisdiction. I remember these figures, and I remember exactly when this table was typed, and I can tell you that this table was produced at the request of the chairman of the Supreme Defence Council for the purpose of regulating the rights that I spoke about earlier. And it says precisely here in the title "Numerical strength of professional soldiers ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, we have to say that we here have certain categories, and underline 16, and I'm going to read for the record the figure under column 7. However, my question is: When was this numerical strength recorded?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read the figures which says that in May 1992 [as interpreted], in the 30th Personnel Centre, there were recorded 2generals, 1.252 officers, which means a total of 1.264. Then we have -- no. My mistake, 12 generals. My mistake. Commissioned -- non-commissioned officers, 1.012, and that translates into the necessary funds. I apologise to the interpreter. We have to correct. I said May 1995. Page 36, line 16. So is this the number of active-duty officers who received salaries through the 30th Personnel Centre in May 1995?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the figure of 2.276 members, but you have to add the soldiers on contract to this figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to make a comparison between this category and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the next page of this document which pertains to the 40th Personnel Centre. Next page, please. That's number 3 in B/C/S. And we have actually the first page uploaded twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the format is similar, so I'm going to read some figures from the table, and you will tell me if I am correct or not. And says that in May 1995, in the 40th Personnel Centre and for monthly net funds, there were, on record, 4 generals, 487 officers, which makes a total of 491 officers, and 434 non-commissioned officers, which makes a total of 925.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Registry, let's give a number to -- [microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit D246. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, given that you were working at this particular administration at the time, do you know whether during certain periods after salaries had started being paid to these members of the VRS and SVK through the ministry, were there any suspensions in these payments?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see document P1870.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, 27 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. It's 1870. Do you have it on your screen? Can you see it, General? If not, we shall wait for you to find the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it. 1870?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. What do you know about this document? Let me just say that this came from the Chief of General Staff, Zivota Panic, dated 22nd of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I know a lot, because I had some personal problems owing to this document. The decision of the Supreme Defence Council whose session was attended by Zivota Panic, the then General Chief of Staff on the 22nd of June, 1993, was to suspend all payments to this category of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of category?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can read it under item number 1, and it says, "People in the service of the Army of Republika Srpska." If I can give my opinion why this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Don't give us your opinion. Tell us what you know.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the result of the refusal to accept the Vance-Stoltenberg Plan by the political leadership of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under item 1, it is said that they shall be rendered invalid, and then they mention documents of the SSNO of the 6th of May and the 17th of May. Were these documents the basis for the payment effected to these particular servicemen?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I was, in 1992, in the administration for system and status-related issues, I didn't look at these particular documents, but I suppose that these documents served as a kind of transitional solution for effecting payments in order not to -- in order to maintain continuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have document 65 ter 01258D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please wait for it to appear on the screen. The document we've just seen was dated the 22nd June. This one was produced a little more than a month later. What can you tell us about this document? Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. After the Supreme Defence Council decided to suspend all payments to the listed categories of people, the Deputy Chief of the General Staff, Colonel-General Dragoljub Simonovic, personally addressed the Supreme Defence Council and asked that for the sake of the existence and -- of these people for this ban to be lifted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to go to paragraph 2 of this document, which reads: "Due to the grave consequences vis-a-vis the financial situation of the families of these men and as approved by the FRY Supreme Defence Council at a session held on the 19th of June, 1993, the federal defence minister, pursuant to his authority, decided to make advance payments of salaries to these men as compensation in the amount of 70 per cent." What's your comment on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that I was facing a great deal of difficulty as head of the administration for the status-related issues - and I'm sorry I'm expanding on this - I said that I was facing a great deal of trouble because families kept coming looking for solutions. There was a certain amount of pressure. The administration of the system and status-related issues in the General Staff of Yugoslavia initiated a meeting of the Supreme Defence Council several days later, and the federal defence minister was ordered to make a decision, and the compensation amounted to 70 per cent as stated here. Furthermore, in the following paragraph, if I may, the deputy commander of the Chief of Staff of the VJ, in view of the galloping inflation that we discussed yesterday, asked for salaries to be brought up to a certain level and that was the spirit in which he addressed the Presidency of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document shall be assigned Exhibit 247, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if at any point over the following period salaries were no longer paid to these persons and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did that occur, and what can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a similar situation that occurred, and I hope you don't mind me not being able to remember the exact date, I think it was sometime in August 1994. Again, because of the non-acceptance of the peace plan by the Contact Group, the Supreme Defence Council decided that the salaries and all payments being made to these categories of persons should be stopped. This agony went on for a full five months, and I had never in my life faced a crisis as severe as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because of all the contact with the families?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The families kept coming to the ministry and wanting to speak to whoever was in charge of the salaries. They thought I was in charge of all of that. I apologise for saying it like this, but it was really a very hard time for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 65 ter Defence list 00829D.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision of the federal Defence minister, Pavle Bulatovic, dated the 6th of February, 1995. What can you tell us about this, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decision of the federal defence minister, as you pointed out yourself, was adopted on the 6th of February, 1995. In the preamble he refers to his own powers, talks about Article 87 on the Law on the Yugoslav Army and Article 29 on the Law on the Financing on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This is the relevant ministry that has the power to pass such decisions and to regulate all the salaries and the salary system for professional members of the army. This decision is on the entitlement and amount of financial assistance for the family, and I have to stress that, of a professional member of the Yugoslav -- or professional members of the Yugoslav Army assigned to the 30th Personnel Centre, meaning of the VRS. May I comment on this decision? It prescribes the exact amount of financial aid to these families. Their survival was at stake. Their livelihood was at stake. Professional members of the army, professional soldiers or civilian employees of the army working at the 30th Personnel Centre. If you go to paragraph 2, it talks about personal earnings and salaries that a professional member of the Yugoslav Army and based on which the aid may be granted to their families under the Law on the Army, salary according to rank, according to position under the establishment, military supplement, and all the other elements that made up a soldier's salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We might as well use this as a good example to clarify something that you said earlier on and that I don't think tallies in its entirety with what it says. You said the reference here is to the members of the VRS; although in Article 1, we see mention there of the VJ. My question is: Why is the term "VJ" being used here in reference to who you think are members of the VRS, as a matter of fact. Can you please elaborate on that, sir? Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons in question are people whose files are in the 30th Personnel Centre. The men who following the withdrawal of the JNA remained in Republika Srpska. These men were assigned and were awarded posts in the VRS, whereas their families remained in the territory of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why does this document make no reference in its title to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason we don't see any reference there is also the fact that such information needed to be secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be received, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's accept this document as evidence. Please, Registry, give them a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this document shall be assigned Exhibit D248. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about active-duty officers of the JNA? What was their situation vis-a-vis their entitlements to housing and accommodation, and then later professionals working for the VJ, and who made these decisions?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who -- who was in charge of taking decisions regarding the tenancy or housing rights of the officers of the JNA and then later the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question warrants a somewhat brief answer, which is exactly what I'll try to do. The regulations governing such issues as housing would have been under the defence ministry, specifically the administration for status-related issues and system issues. As for any loans that are granted, flats that are awarded and the appropriate records reflecting that, that would have been under the garrison command. This sort of thing would have been down to the garrisons of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that flats were distributed and all of this was planned within these garrisons. And it went on like that up until 1995. That was one way. When the Chief of the General Staff realised how complex the situation was, and this is something that we explained yesterday, we talked about the mishaps, the hardship and the circumstances surrounding all of this, and in order to leave everybody on a legal footing in a legal sense, give everyone the same right, he decided to change tack and deal with these issues in the VJ in a completely new way. He, therefore, issued an order in 1995, establishing the administration for housing issues which was attached to the General Staff of the VJ. There was this new system of dealing with housing issues, and I sort of sensed that that is what you want to hear from me. This new system was entirely different from the old one. Perhaps you'd like me to go on explaining this. The administration for housing issues of the General Staff of the VJ is an independent administration within the General Staff. It is directly subordinated to the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ. The Chief of General Staff's idea was to see fewer complaints in the future being voiced by the "down and outs," as I called them yesterday. And also to make sure that there was more fairness and justice in the way housing issues were resolved. One thing I can tell you, during the three years that we grappled with these issues and tried to resolve them in this way, we managed to dampen the blow, soften the blow, lessen the impact of these problems and also to put the entire thing on a more equal footing legally, giving people fair treatment. What were the main principles behind this, and what were the criteria confirming what I've been telling you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think we need to go into that right now, sir. I just wanted you to tell me about the general framework, how it worked before. You said the Chief of the General Staff. Who was the chief of the General Staff at the time when the administration was established? Part of the General Staff of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about members of the VRS who went through the 30th Personnel Centre pursuant to General President Lilic and exercised their rights, did they have any access to this new housing system?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That was a right associated with their status in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When did the personnel centres cease to operate?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My previous answer I talked about the 40th Personnel Centre, saying that it ceased to operate when I became chief of the Personnel Administration. According to my knowledge and my records, the 40th Personnel Centre was abolished at a meeting of the Supreme Defence Council. It has been 20 years, after all. My memory is not at fresh as it used to be, but I believe this was sometime in late 1995. The final decision came in 1997 concerning the personnel centre.
