The abolition of the 30th Personnel Centre was passed by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Dr. Kostunica, on the 28th of March, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You went to the General Staff in late December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please go back to D200 MFI. This is something that we did with General Simic, the order on the competence of the organisational units of the General Staff, and then we went through this with General Simic concerning his own sector. And I think now we have a good witness here to briefly go through this sector. Page 19 in the B/C/S. The English translation that we've got -- it's in e-court by the way. 1D11/0310.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the Usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's towards the very end. It's a somewhat lengthy document. Have you got that sir, General?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I heard rules and actually it says "Order."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my mistake. I'm sorry. Let's go straight to item 21 sector for recruitment for mobilisation and system-related issues. Have you got that, General?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not yet. There's quite a bit to wade through. What page number did you say, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 32. The legibility's poor, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the sector. I'm sure I'll track it down eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You'll find the sector under Article 21.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I've got that, but I can't see a thing, to be honest. I'm, indeed, sorry, Your Honours. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is from 1992. My question is: Was this, in fact, the case in 1995? What about the sector for recruitment, mobilisation, and system-related issues because that's what it was called at that time. Was the name kept later on in 1995?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologise, and I don't mean to be offensive, but this is an order on the competencies, dated 1994. What I've got --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're quite right, sir. So what was the sector called at the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing you see here in this document. The name never changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it have a personnel administration at the time? The third administration, a legal administration, and a department for IT support.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. Sorry to interrupt, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification. The question was: "Did it have a personnel administration at the time?" That's at line 19, Your Honours, and I'm just not certain what time my learned friend is referring to. We've got -- if you go up two or three questions, we're talking about 1992, 1995, and the order dated 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I'm grateful to my learned friend, Mr. Thomas. I'll be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, when you came to the General Staff, you were at first in the housing administration, and then towards the end of 1995 and then onwards, whilst you were in the General Staff, did this sector has -- have these parts that I already mentioned, i.e., the personnel administration, the third administration, the legal administration, and the IT support sector?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning 1995, 1996, and 1997, my answer is yes. When I came at the head of the personnel administration in 1998, it was still called the sector for recruitment, mobilisation, and system issues. However, in early 1999, the housing department was attached to this -- the housing administration was attached to this sector. I just wanted to clarify this. But the name was still the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us briefly what were the functions of the personnel administration, in particular with respect to what they say, elaboration of basic principles of personnel policy. What was this administration doing, actually, and, in fact, with regard to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's on the next page in English, and this is for the benefit of the Bench.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to give you the shortest possible answer because there are lots of tasks and functions involved. So in a nutshell, the personnel administration had the following functions: It's basic and main function was to provide personnel support of the VJ, and it is part of the General Staff of the VJ. That meant that the personnel administration was a tactical wielder of the highest order in terms of providing and recruiting personnel. When I say recruiting personnel, that means recruiting professionals to join the army, organising education system and deciding where students are going to go, to which academies and schools, then announcing vacancies for teachers, then for students. And this is very important. They were expected to prepare plans for annual or six-month plans for personnel training and education. After people finish academy, it is their duty to assign them and deploy them to the units and institutions of the VJ. It was in charge of providing and running an information system for recruitment, which was called PERCEVIC [phoen]. That's an acronym which stands for personnel records. And that would be all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the legal administration involved in?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legal administration of the General Staff of the VJ is a professional organ that carries out duties within the scope of responsibilities of the Chief of General Staff that refer exclusively or, in general, to the following issues: Their duty was to harmonise certain enactments, training rules and all other enactments that, under the Article 5 on the Law on the VJ, fall under the jurisdiction of the Chief of General Staff. They were also responsible for preparing solutions, second-degree solutions, in -- according to the Law on General Administrative Order Proceedings, and these were signed by the General -- by the Chief of the General Staff. They also supplied opinions and suggestions regarding proposals and drafts for certain enactments that were within the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Defence and the General Staff that were drafted in this administration in order to elicit certain opinions from other administration regarding certain issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know how technically it would be best to enter this into evidence. I think it would be better if we link it with the existing document, and we should, on the other hand, maintain the MFI designation, because we haven't received all the translations yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That sounds like a sensible proposal, Your Honours. And in any event, I would defer to the opinion of our Legal Officer, the Court Legal Officer, on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would then propose for the English translation of this part of the document that exists in B/C/S to be attached to the existing translation and that it maintains number D200 MFI, because it hasn't been translated in full yet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we are now going to -- back to the period when you were serving in the General Staff of the VJ and when you were at the head of the personnel administration and when the 30th Personnel Centre was disbanded. Do you know what were the consequences for the people who had exercised certain rights through the 30th Centre after the centre was disbanded and how they managed to exercise they -- their rights in the aftermath of that?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One should bear in mind one fact here, and that is that you have an organisational unit which used to live and then it ceased to live. To form a personnel centre, a decision from the highest level of command and control of Yugoslavia was required. This decision was taken by the President, Lilic, as the Commander-in-Chief. His successor was Dr. Kostunica. As president and Commander-in-Chief, he passed a decision to disband the 30th Personnel Centre. As I said before, I think that took place on the 28th of March, 2001. So this is when the life of the personnel centre ended. You asked me what happened next. Since we are talking about the Army of Republika Srpska, solutions were sought at the highest political levels of different countries, that is to say the FRY, Republika Srpska, and their respective ministries and General Staffs of -- the Main Staff of the VJ and the VRS and the defence ministry of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you involved by virtue of your position in that process and do you know what happened next?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am going to put a document on the screen, and then I'll ask you what happened next.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we please have Defence document 0064D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's an agreement of 12th July 2001, relating to the settlement of status-related issues of members of the military forces.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you to comment on this as soon as we have the document on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, the documents which I'm calling now is 65 ter for Defence 00643D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, what can you tell us about this document? What do you know about it and what effects it produced?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an agreement on the manner of resolving status-related issues of members of the 30th Personnel Centre and on the financial aid of the Federal Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. Since you mentioned the effects, the effect was that an order was issued by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to abolish the personnel centres. In the preamble of this agreement, it is specified on the basis of which documents this agreement was concluded. I'm going to say that that was based on the agreement on establishing special parallel relations between the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Republika Srpska, concluded on the 5th of March, 2002. utterances.text: I'd like to move on to an altogether different topic. Actually, the legal provisions of both laws, the law on the VJ and the Law on the VRS. I've those two ready. utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got that.

utterances.text: What kind of statuses are there under the law within the service in the VJ. Without going to the law itself, could you please explain, sir, in very general terms.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following statuses are envisaged by the Law on the VJ: Persons appointed to a duty, persons doing an Stadj [as interpreted] with the army, persons who are available, persons who are being trained, and persons on sick leave and receiving treatment, medical treatment. Also, persons who were dismissed from their duty post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are these same solutions envisioned by the Law on the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That clarifies that matter, Your Honours, but I wonder if I could have the assistance of my learned friend on what should be on page 60, line 2.

utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, Witness, what statuses in service or within the service does the Law on the VJ envisage? Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Law on the VJ regulates the statuses as follows: Appointment to duty, military trainees, sick leave and medical treatment, training and education, and dismissed from duty. I may have missed that one the first time around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please have Article 52 of the law displayed on our screens now. In the B/C/S this is page 5. Just a minute, please, sir.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 13 in the English, Your Honours.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which article for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fifty-two. I will not be reading this article out loud, but I do wish a concept or two clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to have this displayed also for the benefit of the interpreters to see what the translation appears to be here. Paragraph 6 talks about the statuses in the service of professional officers and non-commissioned officers, or service status. The English that we have in this document is "service status." Another important thing that needs clarifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, General Nikolic, what exactly is "service status"? What is "service status" as opposed to "service situation" or "condition"? We seem to be facing a certain amount of confusion with the English again. I'm not blaming the interpreters at all. General, could you please explain in your own words and then we'll move on to the actual legal provisions.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation in service, briefly, means that each person, member of the army, the VJ in this case, must be in one of these situations or conditions in the service in order to be able to exercise their entitlements under the rules of service that apply to that army. By way of an example, what exactly does this mean, this service situation? Appointment to duty, for example, or assignment to duty. Every professional officer or NCO is assigned to a unit or an institution, appointed to a particular duty or an establishment post which is envisaged for that establishment post under the establishment and envisaged for that rank. What elements does their salary depend on? We heard that that depends on these persons being assigned to a particular position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under the law, what are the relations, the service relations, that exist?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the relations in the service, according to the law, is the relation between a subordinate and a superior. A superior is an individual who is in command of a unit or an institution in which his subordinate is deployed or assigned. So he's in command of a unit or an institution where certain individual is assigned to and is subordinated to him. That would be the briefest possible explanation without resorting to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it possible for any individual in the service to be in two chains of command at the same time?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there is not a single country in the world, as far as I know, and I read a lot, I mean not a single army in the world can have an individual who will have two superiors. Each individual is exclusively in a single chain of command, and he can only have one single superior. This provides to secure the principles of the unity of command and subordination, subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look together at Article 8, paragraph 2 of the Law on the Yugoslav Army. That's page 2 in B/C/S and page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's just wait for it to appear on our screens. Article 8 reads: "Service in the army shall mean the carrying out of military and other duties in the --"

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we discussed this article, we discussed an example, and we would like to use your example to explain to the Trial Chamber the meaning of this. You were a colonel in the Army of Yugoslavia while you worked in the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in the ministry, were you in the Army of Yugoslavia or were you outside of the Army of Yugoslavia, pursuant to this particular article of the law?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of Article 8 is extremely precise in its definitions. You asked me about my case. In 1984, I left the chain of command of the VJ, and I entered the ministry, which was called at the time SSNO. From that moment on until my return, my direct superior was Milos Kosic, Zunic, and the minister of defence. All the orders I carried out in this ministry, including all --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just slowly. We will take it step-by-step. Did you exercise your rights as if you were a member of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the period while you worked in the Ministry of Defence, and you mentioned who your superiors were, who was the only one to appoint you, to dismiss you, or to transfer you?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively my superior in line with the rules about the competencies of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "my superior," you mean the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within the chain of command of the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to the Law on the Army, was it possible for you to rejoin the VJ without the consent of the minister of defence or your direct superior within the chain of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was supposed to be assigned to the General Staff of the VJ, the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ had to ask approval from the minister of defence for me to be transferred to the General Staff. Once this approval was given, only then could I be assigned to the VJ and reinstated into the chain of command of the VJ. By the way, if you may add, all my grades while I worked for the ministry, which is one of the elements for resolving service-related issues in terms of promotion, advancement, additional training, et cetera, depended exclusively on my superiors from the ministry of defence while I worked there. And it was minister of defence himself who wrote grades for me and my performance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Has there been any suspicion of you having committed some disciplinary infringement while you were in the Ministry of Defence? Whose duty was it to institute disciplinary proceedings against you?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on the Yugoslav Army, only minister of defence could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us specifically which article of the law on the VJ provides for the jurisdiction for disciplinary procedures against people who are outside the VJ?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer, but we can look from Article 160 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that you're already tired, and if I help you, I hope that the Prosecutor won't mind. Can you please look at Article 158, and could you comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, it's page 14 in B/C/S and page 39 in English. Article 158.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's linked to Article 152, but there is no need for us to look at it. It contains some general provisions. However, I'm interested in this particular article. Can you tell us what it says?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 158 of the Law on the Yugoslav Army says that the authorisation from Article 152 that has the chief of -- the Chief of General Staff of the VJ and which pertain to resolving service relations of professional soldiers and civilians assigned to the federal ministry of defence and units and institutions subordinated to it shall be carried out by the federal minister of defence only or a commander authorised by him. If I may clarify this further. In Article 152, paragraph 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back one page so that the Trial Chamber can follow. We'll have to wait for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 152 stipulates the authorities and powers of the Chief of General Staff. So I'm reading -- or, rather, interpreting item 2, 4, 6, and 7. Number 2 reads: "Promote professional and reserve non-commissioned officers and officers up to and including the rank of colonel." What does that mean? That means that all members of the VJ who are serving with the Ministry of Defence up to and including to the rank of colonel are subject to promotion by the federal minister of defence. Item 4, Chief of General Staff: "Appoints and transfer professional non-commissioned and commissioned officers up to and including the rank of colonel and issue decision on their service." Which means that it has been explicitly provided that all the situations in the service shall be decided by the minister of defence up and including the rank of colonel. Next item 6, which refers to -- which is being referred to in Article 180 -- 58: "Decide on the termination of service in the army of professional non-commissioned and commissioned officers up to and including the rank of colonel." And Article 153 pertains to civilian employees of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So to recap, all these situations have been very precisely listed in Article 152 and to which Article 158 refers, all these authorities are given to the minister of defence or, rather, delegated to the minister of defence instead of to the Chief of General Staff. I asked you about disciplinary procedures, and, in that respect, can we look at Article 181. Yes. 181.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm grateful to the Registry for being quicker to find their bearings than I can. So let us wait for the English version to appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So towards the bottom of the page you can see it. General, who is authorised to institute disciplinary proceedings against employees of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have the mention of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer slowly, if possible. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: No interpretation of the -- please. I don't see interpretation for the last sentence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, the interpreters are a little bit tired, and you are getting faster and faster. Can you please repeat your whole answer to my question: Who was authorised to institute disciplinary proceedings for the employees of the Ministry of Defence as provided by in article.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was within authorisation of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were in the Ministry of Defence, if God forbid you committed a disciplinary breach, was anyone else allowed to institute these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where these organs were conducted, these proceedings were? Were they part of the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to -- to bring the perpetrator of a disciplinary breach before the military disciplinary court, it is up to the minister of defence and commanding officers of the organisational units that we mentioned yesterday.

utterances.text: General, what we have read, these provisions in the law, were these solutions also a form of adapting the provisions that pertain to VRS and SVK officers when we talked about the personnel centres?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe I didn't understand your question correctly. Whether they were adjusted or adapted, yes, because there were military disciplinary courts.

utterances.text: General, we are not going to go into the issue of military disciplinary courts. Let me repeat my question. utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat if that's what it takes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. No need.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my understanding of the question is correct, you said, Why. Over the course of my evidence, I explained why. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but that was not at all my question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Can the witness please be asked to, before we proceed, to face the make phones so that we can actually hear him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Carefully, General, please, brief answers. I know you're probably very tired. About what the officers of the VRS and the SVK? Were they part of the VJ's chain of command from the moment they joined those other armies on?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to have some of their rights and entitlements recognised, rights -- the same rights as if they were members of the VJ, was their status likened or compared to those who were outside the VJ yet still enjoyed certain entitlements under the law? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Right. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd simply request my learned friend not lead on this topic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Let me have a look. I'm receiving suggestions that there is a problem with the interpretation and also there is an objection by Mr. Thomas. I think the best idea might be for me to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A minute ago I asked you a question about whether those men were in the chain of command of the VJ. You said no; right?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please listen to my question: Under the law on the VJ, there were certain persons who were not within the framework of the VJ. Were the relations -- their service relations regulated as if they were members of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there certain persons -- listen to the question, General. There were certain persons who were outside the VJ, not members. Were their service relations regulated in the same way as if they were members of the VJ or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, leading. Same objection, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think this is leading. I gave the a witness choice between two possible answers. I said, Yes or no. I'm not leading at all, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I maintain that the question is leading, Your Honours, because he is providing all the signals to the witness as to how he should approach the answer to the question, how he should liken these individuals to others, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think we'll just keep confusing the witness. It's best for me to rephrase the question. I really think my question is not leading, but I'm afraid this might lead to further confusion on the part of the witness, which is certainly something that I'm trying to avoid. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under the Law on the VJ, were there certain categories of persons who were outside the army, not members of the army, and yet they had -- and yet they had the same entitlements as though they were actual members of the army? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours, that's another leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have read that article of the law. We went through it with the witness. We all know what this is about. I don't think this is in any way leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas has expressed that you are giving certain tips to answer the question in the way you expect. Is there a way to formulate the question in the most simple and direct manner without anticipating or indicating any answer to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand the witness's allegations in the light of the witness not being offered a choice in terms of answering. I think my questioning was proper. I actually offered two choices and the witness gave an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, during the previous session we talked about the personnel centres and all that. You mentioned the word "assimilation" or "harmonisation." What exactly did that word refer to, harmonisation of laws? I hope that this is a proper way to put the question.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assimilation and harmonisation means that entitlements owing to someone's status can be exercised. This Article 53, paragraph 2, of the Law on the VJ. This is entirely unambiguous as it states the following: "Professional officer or NCO assigned outside the army has all the entitlements and obligations incumbent upon a professional officer or NCO assigned to a post within the army, unless otherwise stipulated by this law." I'm not sure if that answers your question in a satisfactory way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Indeed, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the B/C/S page 5 and the English page 13 pulled up on our screens so we can look at what you've just told us in your explanation. Article 53, paragraph 2 of the Law on the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We talked about harmonisation or assimilation. Can you tell the Court what you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apology to the interpreters. I have been receiving suggestions, and I would propose a different word for "podobrivenje [phoen]" in relation to what was actually written in paragraph 5, line 16. I think the term "recognising" was used previously. Mr. Guy-Smith is telling me that the interpretation is okay and that it works in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This means that this person has all of the entitlements. This person, whose rights are recognised, any entitlements of a professional officer or NCO. The right to a salary, the right to accommodation, the right to various supplements and benefits and any other right and entitlements that this person enjoys under the law on the VJ. As for the obligations, this person must display the conduct of a professional officer. As an officer, this doesn't mean that he can do anything else. He must, at all times, act in the spirit of a [indiscernible] as a professional military officer, in the briefest of terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A while ago we talked about service situations. Let me ask you about something else. We were looking at the provisions of the law on the VJ. Do you perhaps know whether these issues and terms were regulated in a different way in the Law on the VRS and the Law on the SVK?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are entirely identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have Defence document 65 ter 00389D?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, can you find a hardcopy of this document? It's marked 389D. It's an order on the appointment of Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it. I've found it with the assistance of the Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decree of Radovan Karadzic, president of Republika Srpska, of 16th December 1992.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On appointment as per peacetime and wartime establishment of Manojlo Milovanovic, can you tell me what is this decision based on?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see from the preamble what the basis was to issue such a decision by Radovan Karadzic, president of Republika Srpska, which reads decree number this and that, the date, and then it reads: "Pursuant to Articles 11 and 369 of the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska (Official Gazette of Republika Srpska, number 7/92)."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to this document, Manojlo Milovanovic was member of which army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he has been promoted by the person envisaged in the Law of Republika Srpska, I would say that he was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it possible for one and the same individual to be in two armies concurrently?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I make a joke about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible for any single individual to be in two armies at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is mention here of some numbers on the right side. I know this was produced by the army, but, generally speaking, can you tell us once an individual receives this kind of decision on appointment, what do these figures signify? Could he occupy a number of establishment posts or could we have multiple persons occupying the same post?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each order on appointment contains it's basic elements which are listed as kind of code numbers on the right-hand side, and that is whether he or she's being appointed or is he going to act as a stand-in; to which unit is he being appointed to; his rank per establishment; next his position group in order to give him an entitlement to certain salary, a military speciality, which is a prerequisite for appointing someone to a certain post; current duty, rank establishment and position group; and finally the duty station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Please accept -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the general has just referred to the current post and current garrison from which General Milovanovic is being transferred in this particular order, but we can't see that on our screen, and I'm just wondering if Mr. Registrar or Mr. Usher could please scroll down so that we can see the garrison and the location, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we can see now the general has read. I would suggest that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's accept the document into evidence. Please, Registry, let's give it an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document had been assigned Exhibit D253. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had some objections to the record, but let's leave it until later. Can we now look at Defence document 65 ter 00275D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, it's 275. It's an order issued by the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska on the 27th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where -- whereby Novica Simic is being assigned as stand-in. General, based on this document, can you tell us the member of which army was General Novica Simic at the time when this document was produced, that is to say in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can deduce that from the language and the reference to a specific article which is 156 of the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, Official Gazette of Republika Srpska number 7/92, which means that he was a member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have a question with relation to paragraph 4, with which reads: "At present, according to the MF," which stands for peacetime establishment, "commander of the corps of the land army of the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, FCHE [as interpreted] which is an establishment rank, Major General PG 07, as of 16th of August, 1991, Belgrade Garrison." General, do you know whether in 1991 the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff of the GA [as interpreted] existed? Just say, Yes or No.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not receiving any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says here that General Simic at the time was commander of the corps of the land army of the 30th Personnel Centre of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, as of the 16th of August 1991. I'm asking you was the 30th Personnel Centre in existence on the 16th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Guy-Smith is suggesting that we be very precise. We are talking about General Novica Simic. When I said General Simic, I wasn't referring to the witness, General Simic, who was here last week. Could I please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's accept the document into evidence. Please, Registry, assign an exhibit number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit D254. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now take a look at document 65 ter Defence 00192D. So this document is marked 192D.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 00192? I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a decision of the commander of the Serbian Army of Krajina of the 27th of September, 1993, whereby Milan Celeketic is appointed as a stand-in in the Western Slavonija Corps. My first question is based on this document: At the time when this document was passed, the member of which army was Milan Celeketic?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no doubt that on the basis of this document, he was an officer of the Army of the Serbian Krajina. And this is additionally confirmed by the foundation for issuing this kind of decision, which is Article 54 of the Law on the Army of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see -- you said that there's reference to certain articles of the Law on the Army of the Serbian Krajina, but a little bit below it says that temporarily assigned by the order of the chief of personnel administration under Article 271 on the Law on Service in the Armed Forces. We see that this document is dated 27th September 1993. Was that a standard format for the officers who are being dispatched before -- dispatched to the VRS and the SVK before the personnel centres had been established?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's accept this document into evidence. Please, Registry, assign an exhibit number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document -- this document shall be assigned Exhibit D255. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's another document that I would like to look together with the witness. It's 65 ter 00178D. It's a decree issued by the President of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have this document. It's still says Celeketic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, there should be exceptional promotion for Novica Simic.

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, which number?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Now I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we have a decree issued by the President of Republika Srpska of the 26th of July, 1993, on exceptional promotion of Major General Novica Simic. What is the foundation for this decision, General?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The foundation for adopting this decision were Articles 36, 40, and 369 of the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General Novica Simic, at the time when this decision was taken, was a member of which army?

utterances.speaker: STAMENKO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can deduce from the document that he was an officer in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have an exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Let's accept the document as in evidence, and please, Registry, assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D256. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have too many documents left, but I would suggest that we adjourn for the day. I will take some time for chief -- examination-in-chief on Monday, and then I will hand over the witness to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General. General, you are still expected to continue to testify on Monday. Until then, we shall adjourn, and please let me remind you that you are still bound by the oath and do not interact, especially with the lawyers of Mr. Perisic. No communication is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: We are now ready to adjourn and to continue our sittings on Monday, the 8th March, in the same courtroom, at 9.00 a.m. Have, all of you, a nice weekend. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
